Electronic Interiors operates from its headquarters in Lewes, Delaware, with satellite offices in Ocean City, Gaithersburg, and Wilmington. The company runs an Experience Center at its main location where clients can tour smart-home demonstrations.

The firm specializes in residential and light-commercial technology integration, including home theater installation, whole-house audio, network and alarm systems, motorized shading, smart lighting, and thermostat control. Technicians handle TV wall mounting, sound-system calibration, and router upgrades, configuring voice- and smartphone-based control platforms.

Customers are primarily homeowners in coastal Delaware and Maryland, as well as workplace clients seeking automation. Testimonials reference installations in Lewes, Rehoboth Beach, and surrounding areas for families and individuals.

The company emphasizes responsive service and clean, on-time installations, as reflected in client feedback praising technicians by name for professionalism and neatness.

The company states that quality parts and on-time delivery are what set it apart from competitors.

name: Electronic Office
old_description: Simplify payments, maximize savings, and get local support for your business.
about:
Electronic Office operates from West Des Moines, Iowa, as a second-generation family-owned business. Current owner Erik Anderson grew up in the company, which was founded by his predecessor, and now leads a team that includes General Manager Kirsten Ingersoll and Account Manager Megan Farley. The firm has built its reputation on local, personalized service for businesses across Iowa and neighboring states.

The company supplies point-of-sale (POS) systems, payment processing solutions, mobile payment platforms, and scheduling tools. Rather than manufacturing hardware, Electronic Office partners with multiple payment vendors to configure and support integrated systems that handle inventory management, sales analytics, customer engagement, and field invoicing. Its offerings are tailored to each client, with no standard facility or production metrics disclosed.

Customers span restaurants and bars, retail stores, contractors, and specialty shops such as bookstores, boutiques, gift shops, pet stores, flower shops, thrift stores, liquor stores, and jewelry stores. The company also serves local markets in Cedar Rapids, Des Moines, Iowa City, Kansas City, and Omaha.

Electronic Office emphasizes its Iowa roots as a differentiator, promoting transparent pricing with no hidden fees, 24/7 technical support, and customized integrations that adapt as businesses grow. The mission centers on simplifying payment processes so owners can focus on serving customers.

name: Electronic Parts Co
old_description: OUR HOURS OF OPERATION ARE 9:00AM TO 5:00PM MONDAY THROUGH FRIDAY
about:
Electronic Parts Company, Inc. was incorporated in October 1955 and opened for business the following month in Albuquerque, New Mexico. The locally owned business began NE, moved to a larger facility on Rhode Island Street in 1973, and relocated again in May 2023 to its current address on Menaul Boulevard.

The company operates as a broad-line distributor of electronic components and instruments, maintaining what it describes as the largest local stock in the area. Its inventory spans discrete passive components, integrated circuits, connectors, test instruments, wire and cable, chemicals, tools, soldering equipment, ESD protection gear, and a range of other items for both professional and hobbyist use. It also holds authorized-distributor agreements for product lines such as work benches, ergonomic chairs, and microscopes, and leverages a supplier network to source parts not held in stock.

Customers include industrial and MRO buyers, dealers, general commercial accounts, and government entities. The sales team assists with component selection and procurement across that spectrum, from professional engineers to hobbyists.

old_description: Leader in service and installation of specialty electronic systems including:
about:
Electronic Specialty Company was founded in 1947 as a locally owned West Virginia corporation in Dunbar, just outside Charleston. Over the decades it has grown into one of the largest electronic systems integrators in the Mid‑Atlantic region, operating from its headquarters on Dunbar Avenue.

The company specializes in the design, installation, and ongoing service of low‑voltage life‑safety and critical‑communication systems. Its portfolio spans fire alarm, security, CCTV, nurse call, school communications, professional sound, access control, acoustical treatment, and parking equipment. A staff of 54 includes 27 factory‑trained and certified technicians who handle system review, budgeting, CAD layout, commissioning, inspection, monitoring, and repair with online documentation.

Electronic Specialty serves commercial, industrial, institutional, and government clients. Concrete markets include hospitals, schools, prisons, chemical plants, and building contractors across the Mid‑Atlantic. The firm works directly with end‑users and design professionals to develop code‑compliant layouts and performance specifications.

The company emphasizes a drug‑free workplace and a substance‑detection policy for all employees. Its stated mission is to be the employer, solutions provider, and partner of choice, offering a single comprehensive source for life‑safety products and certified technical support from initial layout through long‑term maintenance.

Membership in the Acadiana Home Builders Association and the National Association of Home Builders signals an established network within the residential construction trades. name: Electroswitch Electronic Products
about:
Electroswitch Electronic Products operates from Raleigh, North Carolina. The company was established in 1986 as a unit of Electro Switch Corp, which traces its roots to 1946.

The company designs and manufactures a broad line of electromechanical switches, including rotary, toggle, pushbutton, rocker, and thumb-wheel configurations, as well as encoders and indicator lights. Its rotary switches offer spring return, push/pull-to-turn, adjustable stop, concentric shaft, and keylock options; toggle switches range from miniature to heavy-duty; pushbutton switches cover sub-miniature to standard sizes; and indicator lights include panel-mount and MIL-spec versions with press-to-test, watertight, EMI-shielded, and dimmable features. Electroswitch emphasizes vertically integrated manufacturing and offers custom switch engineering to meet specific application requirements. Through acquisitions, the product portfolio incorporates legacy brands such as Stackpole, Shallcross, CRL/Centralab, ASM, Eaton Miniature, OakGrigsby, Gaynor, and CW Industries.

Electroswitch serves commercial and military-specification electronic applications across diverse sectors. Its switches are used in equipment requiring MIL-spec compliance as well as standard commercial designs.

The company differentiates itself through its design engineering staff, which enables custom solutions, and through a vertically integrated production model that controls quality and cost. It also highlights application specialists and technical sales support as key service elements.

name: Electrotech Service Equipment Corporation (ESE)
old_description: Largest independent manufacturer of UL-listed switchboards/panelboards in the NY metro area
about:
Electrotech Service Equipment Corporation (ESE) is based in Long Island City, New York. The company was founded in 1974 by Phil Cuza, initially serving the minority market. In 1987, Joseph Amendolara and Paul DiPrinzio acquired the assets and renamed it Electrotech Service Equipment Corporation. After relocating operations in 1993 and expanding with a dry powder painting system in 2001, the firm transitioned to employee ownership: an ESOP transferred 49% to employees in 2012, and by 2017 the company became 100% employee-owned.

ESE manufactures UL-listed switchboards and panelboards for residential and commercial buildings, producing custom equipment to project specifications. The product line also includes lighting panels, transformers, disconnect switches, submetering systems, busway, fire alarm fused cut-out panels, transfer switches, load centers, apartment distribution panels, low-voltage substations, motor control centers, and surge protection devices. The company operates a fabrication shop equipped with a dry powder coating system and employs a union workforce (IBEW Local 3).

The company serves electrical contractors, architects, and engineers across sectors including commercial and residential real estate, federal government facilities, hospitals, and municipal transportation. Notable project references include JP Morgan Chase, World Trade Center Tower One, Columbia University, Hudson Yards, the New York Mets’ Citi Field, New York University, and the Plaza Hotel.

ESE emphasizes technical expertise in plan review and engineering support to help contractors meet specifications, aiming to exceed expectations on quality, delivery, and cost. Its early adoption of powder coating and employee-ownership model are cited as differentiators in the local market.

name: Elgin Power Solutions
old_description: Elgin Power Solutions specializes in the design and fabrication of custom switchgear for industrial, renewable, and utility markets.
about:
Elgin Power Solutions has operated from Beaver, West Virginia since its founding in 1977. The company began as a provider of electrical power systems and has grown over more than four decades into a manufacturer and engineering, procurement, and construction (EPC) contractor for medium- and high-voltage infrastructure.

The firm designs, fabricates, and installs custom switchgear, factory-built substations, mobile substations, and high-voltage EPC projects. Its West Virginia manufacturing facility produces mobile substations and other equipment, supported by an in-house team of certified welders, electricians, transformer winders, and assemblers. Engineering staff use Autodesk software and 3D modeling to develop solutions that also include power-quality capacitors for power factor correction, voltage regulation, harmonic filtering, and surge protection, as well as explosion-proof products and field service and testing.

Elgin serves customers across the United States in battery energy storage systems (BESS), data centers, government, manufacturing, mining, oil and gas, solar, utility and electric cooperatives, and wind energy markets.

The company emphasizes its 40-year legacy, innovative engineering, uncompromising quality standards, and dedication to on-time project delivery as differentiators, positioning itself as a partner that exceeds expectations and builds lasting relationships beyond the sale.
